2609.25788.title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models
2609.25788.paper_summary: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) promise a paradigm shift toward zero-shot forecasting by eliminating task-specific training. However, existing works often overlook trade-offs between predictive accuracy and probabilistic calibration. This paper presents a benchmark study of six TSFMs evaluated on energy, traffic, and financial datasets. We contrast their performance against statistical baselines and a supervised DL model. The study reveals that while TSFMs outperform statistical methods and supervised models, they are subject to a fundamental trade-off between point accuracy and probabilistic reliability. Specifically, xLSTM architectures provide robust probabilistic calibration across horizons. In contrast, patch-based transformers offer competitive accuracy but face calibration issues at long horizons, while transformer-based models exhibit context saturation points for optimal zero-shot reasoning. These findings offer evidence-based guidance for balancing generalization and uncertainty quantification in real-world deployments.
2609.25788.paper_summary_zh: 時間序列基礎模型（TSFMs）承諾實現零樣本預測的範式轉變，通過消除特定任務的訓練。然而，現有的研究往往忽略了預測準確性與概率校準之間的權衡。本文呈現了對六個TSFM的基準研究，這些模型在能源、交通和金融數據集上進行評估。我們將它們的表現與統計基準和一個監督式深度學習模型進行對比。研究顯示，儘管TSFMs在預測準確性上超越了統計方法和監督模型，但它們在點準確性和概率可靠性之間存在根本性的權衡。具體而言，xLSTM架構在各個預測範圍內提供穩健的概率校準。相比之下，基於補丁的Transformer提供了競爭性的準確性，但在長期預測中面臨校準問題，而基於Transformer的模型則顯示出最佳零樣本推理的上下文飽和點。這些發現為在實際應用中平衡泛化和不確定性量化提供了基於證據的指導。
